title: Localizable bottom-up apartment household load model
description:
A localizable, decomposable bottom-up model of residential electricity demand in apartment dwellings (without electric space heating, electric domestic hot water or electric-vehicle charging), with resolution down to one second. Probabilistic occupancy (a Markov chain driven by a time-use survey) switches appliances with measured power traces, and the seasonal shape is localized by the national standard load profile, so no local time-use survey is required. Demand can be decomposed down to the individual appliance, which enables efficiency scenarios. Reactive power is computed bottom-up as the sum of each appliance's active-power profile scaled by its measured displacement power factor (values from Hannagan et al. 2023), with an optional per-connection-point capacitive offset for non-appliance contributions such as LV cabling. Supports simulation horizons of a day, week, month or year. Includes a PySide6 desktop application and optional (unvalidated) thermal-envelope and pvlib/PVGIS photovoltaic modules.

This is the reference implementation for the manuscript "A localisable bottom-up model of apartment household load profiles with appliance-level decomposition: validation against five independent measurement sources" (Applied Energy).

Restricted validation data (distribution feeder and smart-meter measurements from the distribution system operators) are not included and are not required to run the model.
